scene.prompt: Use case: compositing / architectural-layout edit. Two references have DIFFERENT roles. Image1 is the AUTHORITATIVE BUILDING DESIGN reference: reuse its SEVEN beautiful complete timber/glass/copper buildings, preserving their distinct recognizable architecture and their visual prominence. Image2 supplies ONLY the landscaped campus layout, spaciousness, mountain setting and winding garden paths. Replace image2's buildings with the buildings from image1; do NOT keep the miniature sports/culture annexes from image2. Produce one photorealistic wide3:1 panorama with an open, realistic landscaped campus, no UI. The seven standalone destinations from image1 are: substantial academic entrance pavilion/pergola with teaching pavilions behind; full-size glazed SPORTS pavilion with basketball court; full-size CULTURE gallery pavilion with sculpture and art visible; full-size SERVICES pavilion with consultation desks and maps; BOOKSTORE pavilion with bookshelves; gabled AUDITORIUM with seats; CAFETERIA pavilion and umbrella terrace. EVERY destination must have its OWN detached building, complete roof, visible facade and independent entrance. SPORTS and CULTURE must be just as substantial and legible as the other buildings, never tiny sheds, never attached to or inside Academic. Same applies to Services and Bookstore: separate full pavilions. ARRANGEMENT: stagger them across a generous garden at varied depths, loosely around branching curved paths and planted courtyards. Approximate building centers: Sports x9%, Culture x24%, Academic x43%, Auditorium x59%, Services x70%, Bookstore x82%, Cafeteria x93%. Vary depth clearly (culture/auditorium/bookstore somewhat farther back; sports/academic/services/cafe nearer) without shrinking any to insignificance. Leave LARGE visible garden/grass/path gaps between footprints; roofs never touch; preserve clear silhouettes. The buildings form a loose staggered campus, NOT a straight side-by-side row, NOT a shopping street, NOT equal plots on a line. Slightly elevated human viewpoint like image2, not aerial/isometric. Medium-distance framing like image2: you can appreciate full pavilions and their surroundings; no huge close-up facades cut by the frame. Each pavilion roughly22-32% of image HEIGHT, with broadly comparable apparent sizes. Landscape and air BETWEEN buildings are the purpose, not a huge empty foreground. Foreground garden/path around20% of height, sky/mountains around20%; the university occupies the middle generous60%. Horizontal panorama for manual left/right exploration; no black letterbox bars, no exaggerated vertical extension. Sharp natural plants with coherent leaves, warm copper roofs, timber structure, realistic glass and fine photographic detail. Keep light and mountain character of both references. No labels, signs, words, logos, people, furniture/desk in front of camera, UI or watermark. All seven pavilions are complete and individually identifiable, with ample breathing room.
